key.purpose: Field keys, state captions and stamped controls.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Stamped signal frame at rest; fills on hover. Used for Download, Bind, Finish.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: transparent; color: #E3B23C; border: 1px solid #E3B23C; border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #EDC158; color: #22282E; } .ds-btn-primary:active { background: #C99A2E; color: #22282E; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Silk frame on steel; a 7% silk wash on hover. Used for Verify, Show details, Back.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { background: transparent; color: #E9EBE4; border: 1px solid rgba(233,235,228,0.55); border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 16px; font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: none; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: rgba(233,235,228,0.07); }

components.name: Capability Plate
components.description: The one plate per surface: double frame, a 2x2 field grid with one state lamp each.
components.html:
MODELNemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B — Q8_0
DEVICESystem default
BACKENDLoading…
HOTKEYCTRL+SUPER · device listener
components.css: .ds-plate { background: #262D34; border: 1px solid rgba(233,235,228,0.55); padding: 4px; } .ds-plate-inner { border: 1px solid rgba(233,235,228,0.26); padding: 12px; } .ds-plate-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 8px 24px; } .ds-field { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(233,235,228,0.16); padding: 4px 0; } .ds-key { font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #9AA39B; width: 96px; } .ds-value { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; color: #E9EBE4; } .ds-value.mono { font-family: ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 13px; } .ds-lamp { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #6FAF74; } .ds-lamp.off { background: none; border: 1px solid #9AA39B; }

components.name: Placard, Warning
components.description: The alarm shape: full signal frame, 10% wash, signal ink. No edge stripe, no icon.
components.html: The keystroke device /dev/uinput is not writable — the transcript goes to the clipboard only.
components.css: .ds-placard { border-radius: 0; padding: 12px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; } .ds-placard.ds-warn { background: rgba(227,178,60,0.10); border: 1px solid rgba(227,178,60,0.70); color: #E3B23C; }

components.name: Placard, Failure
components.description: Failures frame in Stop Red while their text stays readable in Fault Ink.
components.html: Load failed — the partial download is kept and resumed.
components.css: .ds-placard { border-radius: 0; padding: 12px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; } .ds-placard.ds-fail { background: rgba(224,115,97,0.10); border: 1px solid rgba(193,75,58,0.70); color: #E07361; }

components.name: Field
components.description: Recessed well with a hairline frame; the frame turns signal on focus.
components.css: .ds-field-input { background: #1D2329; color: #E9EBE4; border: 1px solid rgba(233,235,228,0.26); border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 10px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 15px; outline: none; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: #9AA39B; } .ds-field-input:hover { border-color: rgba(233,235,228,0.55); } .ds-field-input:focus { border-color: #E3B23C; }

components.name: Overlay Pill
components.description: The one floating surface: 90% plate fill, 16px radius, no frame and no shadow — status legend, two-line transcript, level bar.
components.html: TRANSCRIBING…the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog and keeps dictating into the focused window
components.css: .ds-pill { width: 560px; height: 112px; box-sizing: border-box; border-radius: 16px; background: rgba(38,45,52,0.90); padding: 16px 20px 20px; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-pill-status { font-family: 'Barlow Condensed', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; line-height: 18px; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #9AA39B; } .ds-pill-status.is-error { color: #E07361; } .ds-pill-text { font-size: 17px; line-height: 20px; color: #E9EBE4; display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; } .ds-pill-level { margin-top: auto; width: 62%; height: 8px; border-radius: 4px; background: #E3B23C; }

narrative.overview:
Littera's windows are the machine talking about itself. The Settings screen opens on a single stamped plate — model, backend, device, hotkey, one state lamp each — and then disciplined rows of field facts below it. Legends are condensed and capitalised as if silk-screened onto enamelled steel; values are set plainly; identifiers, paths and commands are monospace because they are data. Alarms are placards: a full frame, the tone's wash, the tone's ink. Nothing is rounded, nothing floats, nothing glows.

The use scene fixes the light: someone at a desk, often at night, screen-lit, opening Settings deliberately mid-work to change one setting and close it again; the overlay pill floats over any content at any hour. That forces a dark steel ground with one signal colour, and it forces restraint — the app is a background instrument, not a destination.

The system is deliberately sparse where it can be and explicit where it must be. Every capability the platform withholds has a surface: a lamp dims, a placard turns on, a blocked path names its fix. The world carries colour as information — the signal yellow means "actable or attention", the stop red means failure, the run green means a verified machine state — and nothing else is coloured.
keyCharacteristics: One capability plate per surface, framed twice, never repeated.
Stamped square controls; hover fills, nothing tweens.
Legends in condensed caps; values in Inter; identifiers in monospace.
Lamps and placards as the only state vocabulary.
Flat steel: no shadows, no gradients, no rounded cards.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Exactly one saturated colour exists. It marks what can be acted on and what demands attention; if an element is neither, it is silk, muted steel or nothing.

rules.name: The Legible-Failure Rule
rules.body: Failure text always uses Fault Ink, never Stop Red; Stop Red only frames. A failure must stay readable before it may look severe.

rules.name: The Stencil-Caps Rule
rules.body: Anything that labels, names a section, or reports a state is upper-case in the legend face. Anything that is a sentence stays in Inter at sentence case.

rules.name: The Data-Is-Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for identifiers, measurements and commands; it is never a costume for technical tone.

rules.name: The Flat-Steel Rule
rules.body: No shadow, no blur, no gradient. A surface is defined by its fill tone and its frame; if that is not enough to separate it, the tone step is wrong.

rules.name: The Square-Stamp Rule
rules.body: Radius 0 is the default for anything that sits in a panel. Anything rounded must be small, floating or transient; if it is none of those, it is a defect.

dos: Do state every capability the machine owns in the plate, with a lamp whose colour is the truth of that moment.
Do stamp controls: legend caps, square frames, hover fills.
Do keep failure text in Fault Ink and reserve Stop Red for frames.
Do set keys, identifiers and percentages in their own faces — legend caps and mono — instead of styling prose.
Do leave whitespace between a state and its action: the caption left, the button right.
donts: Don't round a plate, a field, a button or a placard — radius 0 is the contract.
Don't introduce a second saturated colour, a gradient, a glow or a shadow.
Don't use glyphs or emoji as icons; a control names its action in words ("SHOW DETAILS"), and state markers are stencil words ("OK", "FAIL").
Don't stripe an alert; a placard carries its meaning in its frame and wash.
Don't let a disabled control look interactive, and never dim a lamp to hide a state — draw it hollow.
Don't run monospace outside data, and never upper-case prose.
